chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: Hakim ibn Dawud ibn Hakim narrated to me, saying: Salama ibn al-Khattab narrated to me from Umar ibn Ali, from his uncle Umar ibn Yazid, the seller of al-Sabir, who raised it (to the Imam), saying:

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya (may Allah be pleased with him) would visit the grave of al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and say: Peace be upon you, O remnant of the believers, and son of the first of the Muslims. And how could you not be so, while you are the descendant of guidance and the ally of piety, and the fifth of the Companions of the Cloak? The hand of mercy nourished you, and you were raised in the lap of Islam, and you drank from the breast of faith. So you were good in life and good in death, except that souls are not pleased with your separation, and there is no doubt in the hearts regarding you. Then he would turn to al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and say: Peace be upon you, O Abu Abdillah, and peace be upon Abu Muhammad.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited when visiting the grave of Imam al-Hasan according to Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the pre-Safavid tradition of visiting the graves of the Imams, specifically illustrating the intimate familial bond between Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya and the Hasanayn. The supplication emphasizes Imam al-Hasan’s spiritual purity and his status as a 'companion of the Cloak' (Ashab al-Kisa), reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the infallible Imams' elevated station. This practice underscores the theological significance of the grave as a locus of spiritual connection rather than mere burial site.
